Getting started

sshbox runs a fresh Linux container for each SSH session. Install Docker or Podman on the host and start its service before running sshbox.

Download and run

Download the archive for your operating system and processor from GitHub Releases. Extract it and run the binary:

./bin/sshbox

On Windows, run bin\sshbox.exe. Native Windows server PTY support has not been verified; WSL with the Linux build is an alternative.

In another terminal, connect:

ssh -p 2222 anyone@localhost

Any username and password works. Press Enter at the password prompt. The container is removed when you disconnect.

Build from source

Install Go 1.23 or later and clone the repository. The main branch may be ahead of the latest release.

git clone https://github.com/kknxzz/sshbox
cd sshbox
go run .

Run sshbox --check to validate the configuration and runtime, or sshbox --version to display the version.

Configuration

sshbox uses built-in defaults when no configuration file exists. It looks for config.toml in the current directory, then the operating system's standard configuration directory. Use --config path/to/config.toml to choose a file.

Settings follow this order, from lowest to highest priority: defaults, TOML file, environment variables, and command-line flags. Environment variables use the flag name with an SSHBOX_ prefix, uppercase letters, and underscores instead of hyphens. For example, --idle-timeout corresponds to SSHBOX_IDLE_TIMEOUT.

Container settings

  • --image: container image, default alpine:latest.
  • --shell: command inside the container, default /bin/sh.
  • --runtime: container runtime, default docker; use podman to select Podman.
  • --network: runtime network mode, default none; use bridge to allow normal Docker networking.
  • --memory: memory limit, default 256m.
  • --cpus: CPU limit, default 0.5.

Server settings

  • --listen: listening address, default :2222.
  • --idle-timeout: idle limit, default 10m.
  • --host-key: persistent SSH host key path, default host_key.
  • --max-sessions: concurrent session limit, default 0 for unlimited.
  • --log-format: text or json, default text.
  • --audit-log: optional path for connection logs.
  • --session-log: optional directory for raw session recordings, disabled by default.

The TOML names are in config.toml. For example, the --listen flag sets listen_addr, and --host-key sets host_key_path.

Security

sshbox accepts any username and password. Put it behind a trusted access layer such as Tailscale, a VPN, or an SSH bastion. Do not expose it directly to the internet.

Each session gets a new container. No host filesystem is mounted by default, networking defaults to none, and each container is limited to 256 MiB of memory and half a CPU. These defaults can be changed in the configuration.

Containers are not a hardened security boundary. The host runs the container runtime, so keep it updated and give shell access only to people you trust.

Session recordings

Session recording is off by default. If you enable --session-log, the raw data sent and received by each session is stored on the host. Tell users before recording their sessions, and protect those files.

Troubleshooting

Docker is not running

Run docker info on the sshbox host. If it cannot connect, start Docker Desktop or the Docker service and check the active Docker context. For Podman, use --runtime podman and check podman info.

Host key changed

sshbox creates a host key on first run and saves it at host_key by default. Keep this file across restarts. If the key genuinely changed, verify the new fingerprint with the server operator before removing the old entry:

ssh-keygen -R '[localhost]:2222'

Only remove a saved key after confirming the change is expected. Connect again and check the new fingerprint before accepting it.

Packages cannot be downloaded

Containers have no network access by default. Choose a network mode such as --network bridge if the session needs it. Packages installed inside a session disappear when the container is removed.
